name: Turkey Nasi Goreng
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Sweet-soy fried rice with a distinct caramelized profile. Verified source: full recipe, 4 servings, 453 cal / 23.7g protein with egg. Source uses chicken breast; ours is ground turkey, which is cheaper on the board. Different enough from the live Ground Beef Fried Rice Bowls (kecap manis and chili paste base) that I would defend it, but the selector should confirm. | HARVEST: Published nutrition is per serving including the fried egg. Source uses chicken breast; adapt to turkey.
OVERRIDE Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast: TITLE-PROTEIN SWAP + [BUMP x3.0]: source 150 g chicken for 4 (fried-rice garnish scale); house 1 lb turkey breast
OVERRIDE Rice: duplicate 'Rice' header line was pulling a serve-default on top of the real '3 cups cooked' line; 3 cups cooked = 171 g dry
intro_html: Nasi goreng is Indonesian fried rice, and what sets it apart from every other fried rice is kecap manis, the thick sweet soy sauce that caramelizes on the hot pan and turns the whole thing dark and glossy. Fried egg on top, cool cucumber on the side. Each bowl lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Sweet Soy Sauce, 6 oz: ~$1.76. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.23. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $24.67 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.76 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $40.42 across 14 servings, roughly $2.89 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $14.69 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $55.11. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). One bottle of sweet soy sauce is the difference between plain fried rice and this, and that bottle keeps paying you back long after this batch.
shop_smart: Kecap manis is the one thing you cannot fake here, and it is worth the bottle. It keeps for a year in the pantry and this batch uses only a portion of it, so the real cost per bowl keeps falling.
Turkey breast is two thirds of the batch. Frozen roasts are the cheap form, and the clearance shelf after the holidays is where you should be buying turkey for the whole year.
Cook the rice the day before and refrigerate it. Cold day-old rice fries into separate grains instead of a sticky clump, and it costs you nothing but planning.
Fourteen eggs cost very little and they add a fried egg to every single container. That is the cheapest way to make a bowl feel like a restaurant plate.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice a day ahead if you can and chill it uncovered. Cold rice is the entire secret to fried rice that is not mush.
Cut the turkey breast into small cubes and season them with salt and black pepper.
Heat some of the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok over high heat and sear the turkey in batches until browned and cooked through to 165F. Set it aside.
Add the rest of the oil, then the sliced onion, minced garlic, and chopped jalapeno, and stir-fry 3 minutes until fragrant and just softening.
Add the cold rice and press it into the pan, letting it sit undisturbed for a minute at a time so it toasts, then tossing. Do this for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the sweet soy sauce, return the turkey, and toss for 2 minutes until every grain is dark and coated. Taste for salt.
Fry the eggs separately, one per container, and slice the cucumber into rounds and the green onions thin while the rice cools enough to portion. The green onions go over the top of each bowl.
portion_html: Set the pot of fried rice on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is your per-container gram target. Top each with a fried egg, a few cucumber rounds, and the sliced green onions. Every bowl lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.keywords: nasi goreng, indonesian fried rice, kecap manis, turkey meal prep, budget meal prep, sweet soy fried rice
steps: Cook the rice ahead and chill it uncovered.
Sear cubed turkey breast in hot oil in batches to 165F and set aside.
Stir-fry onion, garlic, and jalapeno for 3 minutes.
Add the cold rice and toast it in the pan for about 5 minutes.
Add sweet soy sauce and the turkey and toss 2 minutes until dark and glossy.
Portion by weight into 14 containers and top each with a fried egg, cucumber, and green onion.
